title: Unique identifier transmission in grading flow
description: Student ID is transmitted as part of the data flow from Grades Portal to Assignment & Grading Service, enabling linking of data across system boundaries.
assumptions: Student ID is a globally unique identifier within the educational system.

title: Processing of identified data in grading submission
description: The flow processes identified data including student ID, course, file reference, and requesting role, which directly identifies the data subject.
assumptions: Student ID and requesting role are sufficient to identify the individual data subject.

title: Unique identifier in data flow
description: Student ID serves as a unique reference to the identity of the data subject, transmitted across the data flow.
assumptions: Student ID is a unique identifier that can be used to identify the individual.

title: Data propagation to downstream service
description: Personal data is propagated from the Grades Portal Web App to the Assignment & Grading Service, where it may be accessible by parties beyond the original collection context.
assumptions: The Assignment & Grading Service may have different access controls or retention policies than the portal.

title: Predetermined set of parties with data access
description: Personal data is shared with a predetermined set of parties (Grades Portal and Assignment & Grading Service) that are known at design time.
assumptions: The parties involved in the data flow are fixed and known during system design.

title: Unawareness of data sharing by students
description: Students may not be fully aware that their submission and grading data is being transmitted to the Assignment & Grading Service, including file references and role information.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate the extent of data sharing between systems.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the quality of privacy notices and user consent mechanisms.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The flow transmits multiple data elements (student ID, course, file reference, requesting role) that may exceed what is strictly necessary for the grading functionality.
assumptions: Some of the transmitted data may not be essential for the core grading function.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the specific functional requirements of the grading service.

title: Unique identifier linking through student ID
description: The assignment store contains student ID which is a unique identifier that can be used to link all stored assignment data to a specific student, enabling identification and tracking of individual submissions across the system.
assumptions: Student ID is globally unique within the educational system and accessible to authorized parties.

title: Processing of identified information via student ID
description: The system processes identified data containing student ID, which directly reveals the identity of the data subject (student) associated with the assignment submission.
assumptions: Student ID is stored in plaintext or can be easily correlated with student identity.

title: Quasi-identifier combination in assignment metadata
description: The combination of student ID, course, and submission time creates quasi-identifiers that could potentially identify students, especially in smaller courses or when combined with external data sources.
assumptions: Course enrollment data and submission patterns may be accessible to authorized personnel or through data correlation.

title: Attributable evidence of assignment submission
description: The stored assignment file with student ID and submission time creates evidence that can be used to prevent a student from denying they submitted the assignment, supporting academic integrity verification.
assumptions: The data is stored in a tamper-evident manner and accessible to authorized reviewers.

title: Extended data retention beyond functional necessity
description: Assignment data including student ID, course, and submission time may be retained longer than functionally needed for grading purposes, potentially increasing privacy exposure over time.
assumptions: No clear retention policy exists or retention exceeds the academic term duration.

title: Student unawareness of data collection and storage
description: Students may not be fully aware that their assignment submissions, including personal identifiers, are being stored in the Assignment Store, particularly if consent mechanisms are unclear or absent.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate data storage practices or students may not read them.

title: Lack of student control over data processing preferences
description: Students may not have the ability to set preferences regarding how their assignment data is processed, stored, or shared, limiting their autonomy over personal information.
assumptions: No mechanism exists for students to opt-out of data storage or control retention periods.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The system may process more personal data than strictly necessary for the grading function, as student ID and course information could potentially be handled with less granularity.
assumptions: GDPR or similar regulations require data minimization, and current implementation may exceed functional requirements.

title: Potential violation of storage limitation principle
description: Assignment data may be stored longer than necessary for the functional purpose of grading, potentially violating storage limitation requirements under privacy regulations.
assumptions: No defined retention schedule exists or retention extends beyond the academic term or legal requirements.
